titles.title: FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN THE ENERGY SECTOR OF UZBEKISTAN: DETERMINANTS, DYNAMICS, AND DEVELOPMENT IMPLICATIONS

descriptions.description: The paper aims to explore and analyze the factors affecting foreign direct investments in Uzbekistan’s energy sector. This includes an analysis of how regulatory quality, infrastructure development, economic conditions, and political stability impact investments in Uzbekistan. The paper employs a quantitative method of inquiry. Primary data collection was conducted by surveying 120 individuals from a variety of professions, including those in Uzbekistan’s energy sector, government officials, and international investment experts. Multiple regression analysis and Pearson correlation tests were conducted on primary data collected using a survey instrument validated by Cronbach’s alpha coefficient. The analysis revealed that regulatory quality (β = 0.463, p < 0.001) and infrastructure development (β = 0.341, p < 0.001) are the most influential factors in Uzbekistan. GDP growth and political stability also demonstrate a high level of influence. The model explained 68.1% of the variation in FDI inflows (R² = 0.681). The paper suggests that Uzbekistan should reform regulations and develop infrastructure to establish an investment-friendly climate to attract more foreign investments in Uzbekistan’s energy sector, particularly in renewable and conventional energy projects.Foreign investments in Uzbekistan’s energy sector will improve the standard of living in rural Uzbekistan. The paper is based on a single country case. The analysis of primary data collected by survey instruments may not be representative of all of Uzbekistan. Inferences should be treated cautiously. This paper appears to be one of the first quantitative studies of multiple factors affecting foreign direct investments in Uzbekistan’s post-reform energy sector. This paper contributes to an emerging body of literature on Uzbekistan’s investment climate.

titles.title: Pollution and climate changes. Feedback from space for sustainable cities and communities

descriptions.description:
Cities represent more than 50% of global population and are the main responsible of energy consumption in the world, accounting for more than 70% of CO� emissions deriving especially from energy and transportation sectors (Global Covenant of Mayors, 018). At the same time, also cities are negatively affected by Climate Change in terms of infrastructure, economy (e.g. agriculture), public services, urban planning and food security, all crucial dimensions for sustainable development. In this scenario, urban planners and policy makers are called to identify innovative solution against crucial challenges related to the evolution of city and environment planning and management. Based on the City Sensing [1, pp. 10-13] approach, the 
aim of this thesis is to identify innovative technological approach that can support citizens to monitor the level the air pollutants and carbon emissions through the interrelation of Copernicus satellites, big data and cognitive techniques, in order to improve inclusive and sustainable urbanization and management of human settlements.
Satellites can help cities to become more resilient to climate change in terms of 

? prevention of climate change through the development of risk management plans based on satellite data series
? adaptation to climate change thanks to the issue of ad hoc policies and interventions for each city
? communication of climate change in order to develop an informed decision making which foresees in climate change an opportunity rather than a risk.

The project will present how the combination of different technologies such as satellites, sensors, the internet drives the development of a new model of knowledge based on distributed acquisition of information whose combination with other already available data, provide a detailed, real time, dynamic and accessible framework for planning the future of a city. Moreover, the crystallization of these information within recorded blocks of blockchain can even create ?shared value? where certified data related to emissions and pollutants are associated with an economic value and resold on the market, in line with the carbon crediting system. In this way the pollutants stop being a problem to become for the cities and start being a solution.

titles.title: Supplementary Data for: Drivers of Topography in Fold-Thrust Belts: A Perspective from Central Nepal

descriptions.description:
The supplementary data contain in- and output files of the surface processes models discussed in Eizenhöfer et al. (2026; ‘In-sequence’, ‘Out-of-sequence’ and ‘Out-of-sequence & Climate Change’; Data S1, Data S2 and Data S3, respectively; referred to as Model I, Model II and Model III, respectively, see Table 2 there) including the ECHAM5 GCM mean annual precipitation output used to implement spatially and temporally variable precipitation (Data S4). Individual model runs may require three to four weeks run time on a single, modern core. The current version of the code does not support parallelisation across multiple nodes.

Both Model I and Model II assume spatially and temporally uniform precipitation, in contrast to Model III. Hence, their model set up is similar except that their structural-kinematic and precipitation input differs. The in- and output files can be opened with standard text editing software and contain the following information:

input folder



icecascade.inThis file contains the fundamental input parameters to initiate CASCADE, each of which explained inside the file.

velocity_Whipple_const.txtThe first four lines only become relevant when CASCADE is linked to Pecube-D, which is not the case in this study, hence, can be ignored. The first column contains the timing of deformation steps and their corresponding MOVE-exported point cloud (second column) recording the deformation.

CentralNepal_Precip1.txtThe first four lines only become relevant when CASCADE is linked to Pecube-D, which is not the case in this study, hence, can be ignored. The first column contains the timing of activity of the respective precipitation field (second column).

prec_....datThis file is used by CASCADE to create its 3D precipitation field at given time step in the model based on the constraints provided in the file.




dist_km
Distance along the x-axis in [km]


Precip_m/yr
Precipitation rate in [m/yr]








pts...datThese files are point clouds representing individual MOVE-derived deformation steps.




1st column
Distance along the x-axis in [km]


2nd column
Distance along the y-axis in [km]


3rd column
Elevation in [km] 


4th column
Point Colour ID not used in this study


5th column
Individual point ID used to track node motion relative to the previous and next deformation step





topoRMT_130.datInitial, MOVE-derived topography used at the start of each CASCADE model run.




1st column
Distance along the x-axis in [km]


2nd column
Distance along the y-axis in [km]


3rd column
Elevation in [km] 


4th column
Line ID not used in this study






ouput folder



topo_tec_....datThese files have been formatted te be opened by the visualisation software Tecplot (https://tecplot.com/). Variables are explained in the header of the file.


Data S4 (ECHAM5 GCM mean annual precipitation output) contains readme files for each GCM time slice in their respective folder. Each folder contains global mean precipitation rates for the given longitudes and latitudes.
